prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Reform UK Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Overview
Reform UK argues that the Conservatives have “broken Britain” and Labour would “bankrupt” it. The party promises a “common sense” alternative focused on border control, tax cuts, public service reform, lower energy costs, and cultural change. It outlines rapid “first 100 days” measures plus longer-term reforms, with costings and claimed savings.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; stop small boats with detention, offshore processing, and returning boats to France.
- End NHS waiting lists while keeping it free at the point of use; cut management waste; tax breaks to retain staff; use independent capacity.
- Make work pay: raise income tax threshold to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut energy bills: scrap Net Zero and green levies; expand UK oil and gas.
- Restore law and order and promote British culture, identity, and values.

Key policies by area
- Immigration: Tight cap with health/care exceptions; leave ECHR; bar asylum from safe-country entrants; immediate deportation of foreign criminals; restrict student dependants; five-year residency for benefits; “employer immigration tax” (20% NI on foreign workers, exemptions for essential health/care and very small firms).
- Government waste: End BoE interest on QE reserves; save “£5 in £100” across departments; deregulate retained EU rules; halve foreign aid; improve HMRC tax collection.
- Economy (personal): Lift tax threshold to £20k; cut fuel duty by 20p; remove VAT/levies on energy; cut stamp duty (0% under £750k); restore VAT-free tourist shopping; reform IHT (0% under £2m; 20% above).
- Economy (business): Lift corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20% then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high-street SMEs funded by a 4% online delivery tax; simplify tax and employment laws.
- NHS: Zero basic rate income tax for frontline NHS/social care staff for 3 years; end training caps, debt write-offs for service; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; voucher guarantees for GP/consultant/surgery waits; weekend theatres; “Pharmacy First”; inquiry on excess deaths/vaccine harms.
- Net Zero: Scrap target and renewable subsidies; fast-track North Sea oil/gas and trial shale; back SMRs and other technologies.
- Policing/Justice: 40,000 extra police; zero-tolerance; expand stop-and-search; harsher penalties incl. mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; raise criminal justice budget; redefine hate crime; build 10,000 prison places.
- Education: “Patriotic curriculum”; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student loan interest; tougher entry standards; more exclusions with doubled PRU capacity; protect free speech.
- Benefits: Tougher conditionality (2-strike job offer rule); face-to-face assessments; push 1–2m back to work.
- Brexit: Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA.
- Defence: Spend 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rise; veterans department; procurement reform; recruit 30,000.
- Housing: Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals for social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; protect leaseholders.
- Families: Transferable marriage allowance (aim 25%); front-load child benefit ages 1–4; single-sex spaces; curb smartphone harms.
- Transport/Infrastructure: Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/most 20mph zones; invest in regional links; 50/50 public–UK pension fund utility ownership; cap standing charges.
- Agriculture/Fisheries: Boost farm budget to £3bn; scrap climate-linked subsidies; “Buy British”; regain control of fishing quotas; ban supertrawlers; expand patrols; rebuild processing.
- Pensions/Social Care: Royal Commission; tackle offshore tax avoidance in care; review pensions; fix Mineworkers’ scheme.
- Constitutional/Culture: Leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; replace Equality Act; free speech bill; reform BBC and scrap licence; reject WHO treaty/WEF/CBDC; anti-corruption unit; new national holidays.

Finances (claimed)
- Savings and revenue: ~£150bn/year plus £10bn from extra growth = £160bn/year.
- Major items: End QE interest (£35bn), departmental efficiency (£50bn), scrap Net Zero/energy subsidies (~£30bn), benefit savings (£15bn), halve aid (£6bn), employer immigration tax (£4bn).
- Costs: Total £141bn/year (personal tax cuts £70bn; business £18bn; NHS £17bn; defence £14bn; others).
